cities: No store of its own in the US · independent shops, and its own site

craft_evidence.makers: John Lofgren & Co. (Japan) named as maker/partner on product pages: Atlas, Heracles, Bantam, Uncle Sam chamois and chambray, Bulldog Wabash, Slub Yarn tee, Deadstock slub tee, Loopwheel Pocket tee, Harvester Henley, Sailor Moku; not named on Railhead, Oilman, Icebreaker, Titan, Arkham, Pacemaker, Border Stripe
craft_evidence.madein: 22 of 23 men's clothing styles state Japan on the product page (fabric milled/knit in Japan, sewn in Japan); Knockabout jacket page states it only in the meta description; no style states another country for the garment (USA only for hang tags, Panama for buttons on Uncle Sam/Icebreaker)
craft_evidence.heritage: Dated, not placed: owner states he founded the brand in 2017; range reproduces 1920s-40s American workwear with dated archive references (e.g. Uncle Sam E-Z Reach 1937, Tweeduroy by Hockmeyer Co.). No founding place on the page.
craft_evidence.process: Yes in part: loopwheel tubeknit with no side seams knit in Wakayama; triple/double-row chainstitching, selvedge gussets, discharge printing, woven tags on vintage shuttle looms, pre-shrunk one-wash; no factory tour or mill named
craft_evidence.reasoning: Product pages name one maker, John Lofgren & Co., and state Japan for almost every style, and the loopwheel tee page names Wakayama as the knitting place and describes the process. No page names a fabric mill (only "Japanese-milled") and nothing says the brand or Lofgren is owned by it; the owner calls the makers "skilled craftsmen and craftswomen" without naming them. Fits the rubric 3: names its maker, owns nothing. Medium confidence. Press (Those That Know interview) places Lofgren's team in Sendai; the brand's own pages do not.

ownership.owner: Bryan Shettig (signs the Who We Are page as Owner; no filing seen)

opview: “My goal is to capture the essence of a bygone era through every garment, piece by piece.” — Bryan Shettig, owner and founder, The Rite Stuff, Who We Are page
